items.text: Title names the main diagnosis or intervention and says case report.
Two to five key words, including case report.
Introduction: what is unique about the case and its contribution.
Main concerns of the patient and key clinical findings.
Main diagnoses, interventions and outcomes.
Conclusion with one or more take-away lessons.
Short background on why the case is unusual, with references.
De-identified demographic and other patient-specific details.
Main concerns and symptoms.
Medical, family and psychosocial history, including relevant genetics.
Relevant past interventions and their outcomes.
Significant physical examination and other clinical findings.
Chronology of the episode of care as a figure or table.
Diagnostic methods used: examination, laboratory, imaging, surveys.
Diagnostic challenges met.
Diagnostic reasoning, including other diagnoses considered.
Prognostic characteristics, where applicable.
Type of intervention: pharmacologic, surgical, preventive or other.
How it was given: dosage, strength, duration.
Changes to the intervention, with reasons.
Outcomes as assessed by clinician and by patient.
Important follow-up test results.
Adherence and tolerability, and how they were assessed.
Adverse and unanticipated events.
Strengths and limitations of the management approach.
Relevant medical literature.
Rationale for the conclusions drawn.
Main take-away lessons in one paragraph.
The patient's own view of the treatment received.
Informed consent was given, and can be supplied on request.
